0.content: King Deshret promised Thoth he would be released from Aaru if humans could supply correct answers to three questions given to the king by the Goddess of Flowers: what causes our rise and fall, what obliterates love and hate, and what determines truth and falsehood. Goudarz answered the first (betrayal and conspiracy) and Makhaira the second (vengeance), and Nefer the third. Nefer's answer, a liar's soul, was her own and was not what the king intended, so nothing changed. In 6.6 she gave the intended answer for all three: time, which broke the curse. Thoth read the king's motive as an attempt to wind back time and return love, hate, right and wrong to their origins.

1.content: Nefer was the third mortal Thoth questioned, after her revenge for the destruction of her tribe. He spoke to her through the cat Ashru and gave her a chess set (a reward for her answer) and, according to a Guiding Note, the power to see through hearts. She refused to believe his tales, gave him an answer of her own ('a liar's soul') rather than the one King Deshret's rules required, and kept Ashru in hope he would talk through him again. In 6.6 Nicole brought her back to Sumeru, where she gave the answer 'time' and freed him. Thoth calls her his chosen disciple. Heryshaf says Thoth likes her because they are alike.

2.content: The three retainers were imprisoned together in Aaru and filled the time with chess. Thoth claims that Heryshaf, a back-seat strategist, advised Sobek badly and that he himself was accused of cheating; Thoth always won, so they stayed friends. Thoth teases them constantly; Heryshaf and Sobek tease him back. In 6.6 Heryshaf volunteered Thoth to take responsibility for opening Aaru, and Heryshaf and Thoth together tell Sobek he is a chess rookie.

3.content: Goudarz, a Tulaytullah noble, answered 'conspiracy and betrayal' and was granted the power to deceive. Makhaira, a Tulaytullah heiress, answered 'vengeance alone' and was granted the power to be loved. Both came to ruin. Thoth will not say whether the gifts or the answers brought it about. Priests recorded each encounter on stone slabs in the ruins.

4.content: Centuries ago Thoth met Zandik, who arrived with an exhausted companion. He found Zandik brilliant but mistrustful, narcissistic and contemptuous, and was relieved when Zandik declined his gift. He then lied: only the descendants of Tulaytullah could leave, and Zandik must not abandon his companion. The companion was a Tulaytullah descendant, but the exit was open to anyone; Thoth wanted to stop Zandik from leaving the companion behind. In 6.6 he recognised the name when Nahida revealed Dottore's plan and said he had seen the man in the desert once.

5.content: Aaru is King Deshret's unfinished afterlife, inspired by celestial technology (and by the Goddess of Flowers). Thoth, Heryshaf and Sobek were imprisoned in it, though their spirits could leave it to possess animals. In 6.6 the Pillars voted to open it, Aaru's Shut in the Mausoleum was used, and it was reprogrammed to replace Irminsul's role. Thoth says it deserves to be treasured even unfinished; when Kaveh calls it both a prison and a monument, Thoth replies that love is the same.

6.content: Thoth calls King Deshret proud and solemn. The king rebuked the Pillars for urging forbidden knowledge, then relented and imprisoned them in Aaru. After Deshret was gone, Thoth says nobody should revere him; the king's gifts are only tools. Thoth quotes the king's promise to the Lord of Dendro of that age that, because of their eternal covenant, he would never be her enemy.

7.content: The Seven Pillars were King Deshret's retainers: Heryshaf, Sobek, Thoth, Bennu, Shesepankh, Hermanubis and Apep (who never appeared in person and rejected the title). Thoth says Al-Ahmar counted the Dendro Dragon as one of them but she never appeared and rejected the idea. In 6.6 Bennu and Shesepankh agree to open Aaru; Apep, already helping Nahida of her own will, is counted as having made her choice ahead of time.

8.content: Thoth once raised cats and their descendants live in his ruins. In 6.1 he spoke through a plump cat in the ruins and told the Traveler it was only 'borrowed'. He sent Ashru to Nefer, where he shared the cat's feelings, and left. Ashru now sits at Nefer's Curatorium of Secrets counter.
